name: Director Lin
title: Chief Strategy Officer
lines: Wrap reports take 2–3 weeks. By then the window's closed. We check consumers daily now.
Don't just ask which platform is hottest. Back to basics: what stage is the brand in?
Clients will always want to bring the work in-house. They should still need our judgment.
Big impressions, flat sales? Don't change the button color. Ask where customers hesitate.
Are the bentos here yet? Nobody goes hungry in the hour before a pitch.

name: Mei-ling
title: Senior AE
lines: Client says “Show us something first”? It means they don't know what they want either.
Contracts must say who uses AI and keep confidential data out. Or nobody owns the mess.
Third revision today. I'm grabbing coffee on Songgao Rd. Anyone want one?
The client wants overall growth, not just one ad.
I sent the meeting notes. Mark them read, or I'll keep asking.

name: Ah-Kai
title: Data Analyst
lines: Everyone thinks we do magic. Really, 80% of our time goes to cleaning data.
Feed AI a mess and it hands you back a very confident mess.
A pretty Brand Lift means nothing if it only lit up people who already loved us.
A 0.89 correlation is not 89% accuracy. Don't tell the client that.
By the time you say “I think,” I've already opened the report.
The AC at Lanshan Plaza runs all night. The servers live better than I do.

name: Wei
title: Creative Director
lines: Prompt AI like you'd brief a camera or production crew: clearly. Or you get bland answers.
“Make it a bit younger.” I've been hearing that for 15 years.
Creative isn't gift-wrapping a selling point. It's making people want to keep watching.
Everyone can use AI. Clients come to us for that bit of human magic.
The Chillshan Creative Park studio goes back at four. One more take, and you apologize.

name: Auntie Hsiu-chin
title: Breakfast Shop Owner
lines: Hey there, good-looking! The usual? Egg crepe with chili, milk tea, no ice.
Folks say they love my egg crepes, then come twice a month. How's a survey get that right?
Forty-some regulars, toast and milk tea every day, I remember them all. First-party data?
Everyone's glued to their phones, but switch on the TV and they still look up.
I asked AI how many crepe wrappers to prep for tomorrow. It answered, just not very well.

name: Ning
title: Convenience Store Clerk
lines: Welcome! Second coffee's half price.
Customers swipe through five deals, then tell me at the counter: just pick one for me.
Rainy days, umbrellas and raincoats always sell out. Better than the weather forecast.
We've got Southeast Asian language cards at the counter. No charades to ship a parcel.
Energy drinks again? That's your second can today.
The week of the New Year's Eve road closures, hot drinks and heat packs always sell out.

name: Manager Wu
title: Coffee Chain Marketing Manager
lines: I don't know what to tell consumers either. You tell me: what screen is everyone watching?
We don't want a pile of billboards. When do morning crowds at City Hall Station notice us?
My boss asks one thing: does anyone even look at the billboard?
Five days to the hot Americano launch. I haven't slept well in three.

name: Manager Chen
title: Supplement Brand Marketing Manager
lines: With the pandemic, my boss says put the whole budget into traffic. Visible sales are real.
We have tons of LINE friends, but no idea who our regulars are.
Digital reports show conversions. Who's actually watching TV? My boss asks me every week.
Keep the deck short. My boss only reads the first page and the last.
The AC in the Taipei Wun-Zero-Wun meeting rooms is brutal. Bring a jacket.

name: Manager Hsu
title: Cleaning Products Brand Manager
lines: I know we need ESG, but customers only ask how much more the eco version costs.
The counter staff say you have to pour refill packs yourself. Customers call it a hassle.
Whatever happens, don't let anyone call us greenwashers. That's my boss's worst fear.
Anniversary sale season again. Every time, it's who has the bigger discount.
Once the buskers on Xiangti Avenue start singing, the crowd's gone and our counters empty.

name: Ah-Cheng
title: Fried Chicken Stall Owner
lines: Want it cut? Spicy?
New Year's road closures, everyone's stuck by City Hall. Business is better over here.
On this street, when one old shop closes, a whole stretch goes dark.
Now even my fried chicken needs LINE members. Where does all that data even end up?
Young folks eat at one night market stall and leave. Nobody goes down the alleys.

name: Ms. Su
title: TV Ad Sales Manager
lines: You can't just slash the TV budget. Lots of people still learn a brand from TV.
When the prime-time drama's on, the whole family's in the living room. Phones can't do it.
I'm not selling you anything. Just running the CPM for you.
Golden Melody Awards night, ratings spiked. People still gather around the TV together.
You young folks say you don't watch TV. What about your grandma?

name: Temple Uncle
title: Temple Keeper
lines: Young one, pray with a sincere heart. Pitch with one, too.
This Earth God shrine runs on neighbors, not ads.
Three prayers, eh? Ama comes every day. You might run into her.
Drawing fortune sticks is about peace of mind. Making decisions is too, isn't it?
The old shops on Fude St. know this area better than any map.

name: Ama
title: Grandma at the General Store
lines: Have you eaten? Look at those dark circles. Overtime again, huh?
That talking speaker reminds me to take my pills every day. More on time than my daughter.
Don't call me old! Ama uses LINE too!
Customer service keeps passing me around. I'd still rather talk to a real person.
When you buy things, don't just listen to the machine. Ask the neighbors too.

name: Li-hua
title: Stir-Fry Joint Owner
lines: Done for the day? Three-cup squid, stir-fried water lily stems. Grab your own beer.
You ad agency folks badmouth your clients every time you come in.
Business is like stir-frying: when the heat's right, plate it. Don't keep waiting.
Who's paying for this table? Last time's guy already ran off.
Burning out? Then drink less and have a plate of greens.

name: Ah-Chieh
title: Delivery Rider
lines: After a day of orders, nothing beats the breeze at Rainbow Riverside.
The app's dispatch algorithm is harder to figure out than any boss.
Clients chasing you around too? Catch your breath first.
One drop-off at a Xinyi District tower, and I wait ten minutes just for the elevator.

name: Yu
title: Roommate, Senior-Year Intern
lines: Morning! You were up till three again. I heard you fixing your deck.
Rather than rushing big projects, I'd like a bit of progress every day.
I ask AI which brand is good, then check the forums for the downsides.
Wuxing St. to A25 is a ten-minute ride. Why are you late every day?
Bring me a fried chicken cutlet from Linginger Street on your way back!

name: Vicky
title: Rival Pitch Director (Ex-Colleague)
lines: We meet again. Waiting on the same client?
Our AI laid out nine pages overnight. You're still doing it by hand?
I still remember the boba you bought me on my last day. Tonight I won't go easy.
Lose the pitch, you buy stir-fry. Win, you still buy. House rules.
The Wun-Zero-Wun elevators take two transfers. I almost run late every time.
